paper_title: On the Complexity of Value Iteration (Track B: Automata, Logic, Semantics, and Theory of Programming)
classifications: Theory of computation → Logic and verification
Theory of computation → Markov decision processes
statement: The exact complexity of the following variant of the problem remains open: given an MDP and a horizon encoded in binary, determine whether there exists a policy achieving some given expected-reward threshold (with no restriction on the actions used to do so).
context: I Theorem 9. All the following problems are EXPTIME-complete: The finite-horizon reward problem for MDPs, and thus also the ValIt problem. The finite-horizon reachability and synchronized reachability problems for MDPs. The powering problem for SLPs and for monotone SLPs. The bounded termination problem for simple counter programs. The exact complexity of the following variant of the problem remains open: given an MDP and a horizon encoded in binary, determine whether there exists a policy achieving some given expected-reward threshold (with no restriction on the actions used to do so).
